In the Draft report, information regarding industrial waste water flows are not revealed. The Final report, therefore, should expand the scope of water and sewerage system to include industrial water usage and discharge.
Regarding drainage systems, efforts should be made to install adequate drainage facilities prior to the completion of the project.
VIII SOLID WASTE
The Draft report reveals that 30 to 40 tons of solid waste would be generated per day and, approximately 10 trucks per day would be needed to haul this waste. To minimize solid waste impacts, it appears that a comprehensive solid waste management program is desirable. Such a program should include pickup truck traffic coordination, easy access to waste bins, aesthetic confinement of bins and prevention of waste littering. The CRA with the cooperation of the City of Cambridge also should encourage occupants of Kendall Square to participate in the existing wast recycling program.
IX WATER AND ENERGY CONSERVATION
Currently, the Commonwealth is actively formulating a water supply policy to relieve increase demands and to ensure adequate water supply for future use. The Kendall Square development presents an unique opportunity to the CRA and City of Cambridge to participate in this statewide effort. The CRA, therefore, should vigorously solicit water conservation measures among the developers and also should help develop such programs.
As required by the Energy Policy and Conservation Act, the Energy Policy Office has proposed a statewide energy conservation program. In view of this, the CRA should incorporate appropriate standards into all development aspects of the proposed project.
X CONSTRUCTION PHASE
Although temporary in nature, construction phase impacts can be among the most severe environmental impacts of any major urban development project, particularly where construction will be stage over a period of several years. This area merits more complete consideration in the final report.
Five aspects of construction phase need to be emphasized: (1) Air emmissions from demolition, excavation and construction will need to be carefully controlled; (2) the ultimate disposal of demolition and excavation debris may pose a problem, particularly in view of the limited availability of approved landfill locations; (3) noise from on-site activity and trucking should be controlled and minimized; (4) potential alterations of the groundwater regime should be avoided to minimize impacts to adjacent structures; (5) steps should be taken to minimize general off-site construction impacts particularly to the Kennedy School and residential areas.
